attempt_history.prompt: Depict Cyhyraeth of Welsh mythology as the explicitly BODILESS moaning spirit, using the documented corpse-light seen along the Glamorganshire coast before a shipwreck. There must be NO human or animal body, face, eyes, arms, legs, clothing, female silhouette, skeleton or invented anatomy. The entity is one coherent supernatural cold blue-white corpse-light hovering above a dark rocky Welsh shore, with clearly emitted luminous mourning-energy strands spreading out across the sea wind and curling into the black air. Make the central light intensely bright, an eerie spectral beacon that radiates its own light and floating magical particles; its surrounding strands subtly suggest waves of a mournful bodiless voice but never form a person. Oppressive terrifying midnight coastal atmosphere, distant rough sea and cliffs, no actual wreck, dying people, corpse or victims. Square premium highly detailed painterly mythological encyclopedia illustration, no text, captions, symbols, border or watermark.
